summary.headline: Balaji Amines Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 36% YoY to INR472 crores and PAT 82% to INR67 crores, though EBITDA fell sequentially to INR106 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR472 crores, up about 36% YoY and up from INR461 crores in Q1, while EBITDA was INR106 crores (22% margin) versus INR121 crores (26%) in Q1. Sales volume rose about 13.5% QoQ to 24,491 MT but was down about 6% YoY. H1 FY27 PAT was INR146 crores, up about 98%, despite H1 volumes falling to 46,078 MT from 53,735 MT. The company commissioned the expanded Acetonitrile plant (1,440 TPM) and the DME plant, and it received PESO approval for DME road tanker valves; brownfield and greenfield specialty chemicals projects have slipped toward FY27 end and Q4 FY27 respectively.

segments.name: Amines (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 6,525 MT. Unit-4 methylamine utilisation is only about 15-20% per management, while Unit-3 ran at about 80%.

segments.name: Amines Derivatives (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 8,974 MT. DMF plant utilisation rose from about 30-40% to more than 50% on DMF prices of INR110-115 per kg. EDA utilisation is about 50-60%.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals (volume)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume of 8,992 MT. DME and Acetonitrile are ramping; Acetonitrile is priced around INR230-240 per kg.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to reach INR3,500-4,000 crores top line by FY28-29, which the analyst had framed as a INR3,000-4,000 crore aspiration.
All expansions, including Acetonitrile, DME, DMF, NMM and the Balaji Specialty Chemicals projects, are to be completed by end of FY27. From Q1 FY28, the focus shifts to utilisation of 80-90%.

Unit-1 brownfield at Balaji Specialty Chemicals (EDA derivatives) is expected to be commissioned by end FY27. Unit-2 greenfield at Chincholi (hydrogen cyanide, sodium cyanide, EDTA) is targeted for Q4 FY27, with some products possibly slipping to February or March 2027.
NMM commercialisation is targeted during FY27.

DME: bulk supply is expected once Road Tanker approval is received (3-4 weeks) and the BPCL LPG-blending approval is in place. Capacity utilisation could exceed 90% with that approval, or 50-55% without it.
Acetonitrile: full capacity of 1,440 MT per month expected in 2-3 weeks; management guided minimum 1,000-1,200 MT per month from December, subject to market acceptance.
DME pricing indicated at INR90-100 per kg currently, expected to be competitive with LPG once methanol falls below INR80 per kg.
capex_capacity: Expanded Acetonitrile plant commenced commercial production in Q2 FY27 at 1,440 tons per month capacity, with improved process technology.
DME plant commissioned; PESO approval received for DME road tanker valves. Road tanker approval expected in 3-4 weeks. 7-8 ISO tanks exported for aerosol use; about 20-25 cylinders sold domestically.

Unit-1 at Balaji Specialty Chemicals (brownfield EDA derivatives: DETA, TETA, Piperazine, AEEA, AEP) is being run in 10-15 day cycles alternating with modifications. Remaining work is small equipment erection, to finish in one or two cycles by January 2027.
Unit-2 greenfield at MIDC Chincholi is in equipment erection and installation, targeted for Q4 FY27.

Di-isopropylamine process improvement reported as yielding positive results. Management also cited a DMC/DMC-PC order from a battery electrolyte client for 500-1,000 MT, with delivery expected from next month.
demand_pricing: Volumes lag because raw material prices are volatile, so the company is booking orders against demand rather than building inventory. H1 FY27 volume fell about 14% YoY.
DMF prices rose to INR110-115 per kg from earlier levels. Management said Chinese dumping had previously made Indian DMF uneconomic.
EDA price improved, but anti-dumping duty recommended by the Commerce Ministry was not implemented by the Finance Ministry. The company plans a High Court writ petition within about one month.
Methanol is about INR61-62 per kg versus INR6 when management began the business. Management expects normal levels of INR26-30. Ammonia is INR80-90 versus a normal INR45-50.
DME demand is mainly aerosol in India (over 50,000 tons consumption) and export; LPG blending is pending BPCL and government approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the DMF plant now that DMF prices have risen, and when will Unit-4 methylamine improve?
qa_highlights.answer: DMF utilisation has risen from about 30-40% to more than 50% at prices above INR110-115 per kg. Unit-3 ran near 80%. Unit-4 is at about 15-20% and management expects 70-80% over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the progress on DMC supply to the battery electrolyte client and on any further capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The client now asks for 500-1,000 MT of DMC and propylene carbonate, against earlier requests of 20-60 MT. Delivery is expected from next month. Further capacity depends on other clients coming on stream; no decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EDA volume not picking up after anti-dumping, and what is the next step?
qa_highlights.answer: EDA is running at about 50-60% utilisation. The Commerce Ministry recommended anti-dumping duty but the Finance Ministry did not implement it. The company plans a writ petition in the High Court within about one month.

qa_highlights.question: What approvals remain for DME LPG blending, and what pricing should be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Valves approval is done. Road tanker approval is expected in 3-4 weeks, followed by BPCL and government approval for LPG blending. Current DME pricing is INR90-100 per kg, which management expects to become competitive below methanol at INR80.

qa_highlights.question: What Acetonitrile pricing should be assumed, and what is the value growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Acetonitrile is at about INR230-240 per kg and depends on raw material prices. Full capacity is expected in 2-3 weeks. Management reiterated INR3,500-4,000 crore top line by FY28-29 even if prices decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Unit-1 brownfield expansion been delayed from July, then October, to year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company keeps the plant running to serve the market and cannot run manufacturing and expansion in the same plant at once. Products should reach the market from January 2027, with possible slippage to February or March.

risks_watch: Brownfield timelines have slipped repeatedly (July 2026, then October 2026, then FY27 end). Unit-1 and Unit-2 commissioning could slip to February-March 2027.
Volumes have fallen YoY, and utilisation is low at Unit-4 methylamine (15-20%), EDA (50-60%) and the existing DMC capacity (about 30%).
The EDA anti-dumping duty stalled at the Finance Ministry, and the company's High Court petition timing is uncertain.
Raw material price volatility (methanol, ammonia) and geopolitical conditions drive pricing for DME, Acetonitrile and DMF. Management said prices could fall once conditions normalise.
Sequential EBITDA margin fell from 26% to 22%. The DME LPG-blending approval is still pending.
Net worth figure was corrected on the call from INR2,023.02 crores to INR2,083.02 crores, so the transcript figure needs confirming.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and the expansion narrative, but cautious and at times evasive on timelines and volumes. Management repeatedly cited regulatory and logistics delays, and it deferred the DME pricing and approval questions to uncertain external approvals.

adds.what: Expanded Acetonitrile plant at 1,440 MT per month (commercial production commenced Q2 FY27)
DME plant commissioned; road tanker approval pending (3-4 weeks)
Balaji Specialty Chemicals Unit-1 brownfield (EDA derivatives: DETA, TETA, piperazine, AEEA, AEP)

growth.why: Management targets INR3,500-4,000 crore top line by FY28-29 (versus INR933 crore H1 FY27 revenue, which is 31% up YoY), backed by commissioned Acetonitrile and DME plants, a DMC order of 500-1,000 MT, and Unit-1/Unit-2 projects due by end FY27 to Q4 FY27, though brownfield and greenfield timelines have slipped and Unit-4 methylamine runs at only 15-20%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 22% in Q2 FY27 from 26% in Q1 (19% a year ago), but management expects DMF/DME/Acetonitrile pricing and Unit-4 ramp to support margins, with pricing that could fall once raw materials (methanol INR61-62/kg vs normal INR26-30) normalise.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Unit-1 brownfield EDA (DETA, TETA, piperazine) is targeted for January 2027, Unit-2 Chincholi greenfield for Q4 FY27, and Acetonitrile is at full 1,440 MT/month, though timelines have already slipped from July to October to FY27 end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Acetonitrile guided to a minimum 1,000-1,200 MT/month from December, DMC order of 500-1,000 MT from next month, and DMF utilisation up from 30-40% to above 50%, against H1 FY27 volume down about 14% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low at Unit-4 methylamine (15-20%), EDA (50-60%) and DMC (about 30%), so near-term new capex is unlikely, but management's INR3,500-4,000 crore top-line target for FY28-29 implies further investment after the FY27 projects are complete.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated INR3,500-4,000 crore top line by FY28-29 (versus INR933 crore in H1 FY27, up 31% YoY), though the call framed it as an aspiration and the figure was raised from a prior analyst framing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Brownfield and greenfield timelines have slipped repeatedly, Unit-1/Unit-2 could slip to February-March 2027, and DME at 50-55% utilisation without LPG-blending approval, which is still pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Unit-1 EDA derivatives (DETA, TETA, piperazine, AEEA, AEP) are expected to reach market from January 2027, Unit-2 products (hydrogen cyanide, sodium cyanide, EDTA) in Q4 FY27, and NMM commercialisation is targeted during FY27.

rows.label: EDA anti-dumping duty via High Court writ
rows.why: Commerce Ministry recommended anti-dumping duty but Finance Ministry did not implement it; company plans a High Court writ within about one month, and EDA utilisation is only 50-60%.

rows.label: DME LPG-blending and road tanker approvals
rows.why: Road tanker approval expected in 3-4 weeks; DME utilisation could exceed 90% with BPCL LPG-blending approval versus 50-55% without it, at DME pricing of INR90-100/kg.

rows.label: Methanol and ammonia normalisation
rows.why: Methanol at INR61-62/kg vs normal INR26-30 and ammonia at INR80-90 vs normal INR45-50; a fall would lift margins but could also cut DMF, DME and Acetonitrile prices.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, the INR3,500-4,000 crore top-line target and Acetonitrile/DME ramp, but cautious and at times evasive on brownfield timelines, volumes and pending DME and EDA approvals; analysts pressed on timing slippage and utilisation.
